summary:
# NOTES: *Dorcas Dene, Detective: Her Adventures* (George R. Sims, Gutenberg #77243)

Single book, 11 linked stories. Narrator = **Mr. Saxon**, dramatist, unnamed in narration, called "assistant" by Dorcas.

## Cast (recurring)
- **Dorcas Dene** (née Lester), lady detective, blonde, soft brown wavy hair, grey eyes. Ex-actress. Disguises: gipsy, American lady, parlour-maid, German frau "Mrs. Goldschmidt", Italian street musician, gipsy race-card seller.
- **Paul Dene**, her husband, blind artist, fair waving hair, pipe (briar-root). Says "council of four."
- **Mrs. Lester**, Dorcas's mother, buxom, grey-haired, matter-of-fact, dislikes melodrama, "speaks her mind."
- **Toddlekins**, brindle bulldog. Once saved a woman by seizing a drunken man's throat; Dorcas got him from police. Dislikes the clock-winding young man.
- **Mr. Johnson**, retired superintendent of police, neighbour, "looked like a jolly sea captain," recruited Dorcas; retired a year before story I.
- **Mr. Jackson**, ex-police sergeant of Penton Street, King's Cross; Dorcas's watcher/inquiry man.
- **Inspector Swanage**, Scotland Yard, knows "the boys" (racecourse crooks).
- **Inspector Stromberg**, CID, foreign-looking dark man, ~38.
- **Karl**, German waiter at Star and Garter, Richmond; **Mr. James**, manager.
- **Guiseppe**, narrator's waiter friend (Strand café), Camorra member.

## I. THE COUNCIL OF FOUR
- Narrator (Saxon) first gave Dorcas Lester a chance: maid with two lines, then small parts ~12 months at West End theatre. Last part: old hag (praised). Left mid-run, married.
- 8 years later, at West End solicitor's office (unnamed Mr. ----), sees Dorcas leave; she's "Dorcas Dene, famous lady detective."
- Case: young **Lord Helsham** (came of age) disappeared. Mother **Lady Helsham** (client) wants no police, fears mésalliance.
- Dorcas takes narrator by hansom to St. John's Wood.
- Her backstory: father an artist, died leaving debts. She earned 2 guineas/week; lived in two rooms, St. Paul's Road, Camden Town. Married **Paul Dene**, young artist, £700–800/yr. House: Oak Tree Road, St. John's Wood. Paul went blind after illness; income ~£100/yr.
- Johnson (neighbour) asked her to help rescue a blackmailed man who fled wife and children. Pay: guinea a day plus expenses. Condition: Paul not told until she tested it.
- Key scene: she asks Paul "How do you think I look, dear?"; he turns blind eyes, lip quivers; she runs out; Johnson at door.
- Home: Paul, Mrs. Lester, Toddlekins. Mrs. Lester warns the dog will kill the clock-winder.
- Dorcas in gipsy disguise: asks narrator to get her a gipsy super job at the ------ Theatre, third act. Meet 8pm.

## II. THE HELSHAM MYSTERY
- Narrator in stalls for third act of gipsy drama. Dorcas (disguised) at stage door; hansom to Grosvenor Square.
- Clue: photo found in Bertie's papers: "To dearest Bertie, from Nella." Photographer Alfred Ellis, Baker Street; "Miss Nella Dalroy in *The Gipsy Wife*." Lord Helsham = Bertie.
- Nella's letter: he "sees no way out," must forget him, left "all that he has a right to leave." Dorcas reads: suicide.
- Council at Oak Tree Road: Paul says fear is motive. Lady Helsham seemed "relieved" at suicide talk.
- Family history: late Earl killed hunting; younger brother **Hon. John Farman** would inherit if no son. Son born a month after father's death, premature. Lady Helsham adopted her sister's little girl; son refused to marry her; girl returned to Scotland.
- Farman: Lady Helsham confined at sister's house, Scotland (sister = wife of merchant captain, sailed to Australia). Farman calls Bertie "a most lovable young fellow."
- Miss Dalroy shows letters; one posted from **Dunkeld**, Scotland.
- Dorcas goes to Dunkeld. Captain's widow (Mrs. ----), old Scotch servant (illiterate), doctor with spectacles, Bertie ill upstairs.
- Widow confesses: Lady Helsham's child was a girl; sister's baby boy swapped in; midwife paid; doctor absent 24 hours.
- Bertie learned he'd dispossessed another; threatened by Lady Helsham; planned suicide, Dorcas staged it.
- Clothes and watch left at **Cromer** (Norfolk) cave. Daily Telegraph: "A Mystery Cleared Up," credits Dorcas.
- Outcome: Bertie to marry Nella, emigrate to America; Lady Helsham to live abroad. Dorcas: "if everybody did the legal thing... very little work for a lady detective."

## III. THE MAN WITH THE WILD EYES
- Narrator's "assistant" role; Dorcas allows stories if clients unidentified.
- **Colonel Hargreaves**, Orley Park, near Godalming (also "Orley Court"). Daughter **Maud**, 25, found by lake, half in water; throat marks, wrists bruised. Story: fainted, then "tramp" attacked her.
- Doctor (unnamed) advises private inquiry. Dorcas poses as trained nurse; narrator as artist sketching the grounds. Inn: "The Chequers."
- Lodge-keeper **Mr. Peters**; wife **Mrs. Peters**: ~7pm man peering through lodge gates, "wild, staring eyes," asked name of house. Arrived by train that afternoon.
- Gardener found Maud ~10pm. Dogs (two mastiffs) bark at side gate.
- Footprints: hobnailed boots (gardener); narrow pointed-toe boot prints (the man).
- Dorcas drops purse at lodge gates to study footprints; footprints match.

## IV. THE SECRET OF THE LAKE
- Dorcas at station: man bought single ticket from Waterloo, no luggage.
- Narrator climbs wall; dogs bark; Peters comes; narrator escapes.
- Dorcas's dream test: calls "Maud!"; Maud answers "Victor!"
- On fowl island: finds felt hat with dent (Peters confirms).
- Photo carte de visite: London Stereoscopic Co., negative 111,492. Erased name on back; small V scarf-pin.
- Name: **Victor Dubois**, Anerley Road, Norwood. Father **Mounseer Dubois**, Professor of Languages, went insane, asylum. Letters in a woman's hand came for Mr. Victor.
- Colonel: Maud had a French master; Crystal Palace drawing class; train incident.
- Wedding ring found in Maud's jewel-box. Search at Somerset House (Daddy Green): marriage **Victor Dubois** (bachelor, 26) and **Maud Eleanor Hargreaves** (21), London, 1891.
- Body found in lake (Dorcas rowing); Dorcas searched pockets first.
- Maud's account: she met Victor, secretly married. He'd been in asylum; came to Orley Park; grabbed her throat; she fell in; he drowned himself.
- Inquest: Victor Dubois, lunatic, drowned. Colonel takes Maud abroad. Mrs. Lester: daughter "fishing up corpses for a living."

## V. THE DIAMOND LIZARD
- July, Star and Garter, Richmond. Dorcas as American lady, silver-grey hair, dark complexion, courier bag. Paul & Mrs. Lester at Eastbourne.
- Party: **Claude Charrington** (~23, son of barrister Mr. Charrington); **Miss Dolamore** (pretty, red sailor-knot tie, red hatband); older bold woman (Mrs. Rinaldi).
- Dorcas is parlour-maid at Charringtons. Client: **Mrs. Charrington** (second wife, mourning for brother who died in India).
- Stolen: diamond & ruby bracelet, diamond & ruby pendant, small diamond lizard. Jewels given by Mr. C as birthday present.
- Claude pawned watch & chain for £10; then had banknotes; fox-terrier Jack. Suspicion on Claude.
- Johnson the footman bets, owes a sovereign. Lady's maid engaged to honest man.
- Dorcas sees the diamond lizard fastening Miss Dolamore's red tie.
- Telegram: "Marble Arch, four o'clock. --DORCAS."
- Miss Dolamore: widow's daughter, comic-opera singer, lodges at Fitzroy Street; landlord **Carlo Rinaldi** (Italian), wife English, the older woman.
- Bracelet & pendant pawned at Attenborough's by "Claude Charrington." Mr. Charrington back in town on day of Richmond.

## VI. THE PRICK OF A PIN
- "The Camorra," gambling club, Soho; Rinaldi member. Narrator gets Guiseppe to take them.
- Ketner's, Church Street, 10pm. Dorcas as German frau "Mrs. Goldschmidt," cameo brooch.
- Upstairs card room: Dorcas spills brandy-and-soda into Rinaldi's breast pocket; snatches pocketbook; finds pawn-ticket for bracelet and pendant in Claude's name.
- Explanation: Mr. Charrington replaced jewels; pricked finger on lizard pin; bloodstain on sheet and key; sleeping wife Mrs. C.
- Johnson: Claude's Leger tip (33-to-1 winner, £200).
- Rinaldi was valet; wife = Charrington's former mistress.
- Sunday, Eastbourne: Dorcas tells the rest. Mr. C visited, confessed. Jewels given to Rinaldi's wife, pawned by Rinaldi. Birthday present from Streeter's: wrong parcel handed by clerk. Charrington had copies made by jewellers, swapped back at night. Wife told "imitation" story.
- Epilogue: Claude engaged to Miss Dolamore; lizard swapped for diamond poodle with ruby eyes; diamond true-lovers'-knot given.

## VII. THE MYSTERIOUS MILLIONAIRE
- Narrator's late arrival; sees nervous lady leave Oak Tree Road: **Lady Anna Barraclough**.
- Background: 25; first husband (ran through money, died at 27 of typhoid); married **Judkins Barraclough** (~45, South American millionaire, arrived 3 years ago) ~1 year ago. Was dependent on brother, Earl of Dashton, whose wife detested her.
- Suspicion: Barraclough a bigamist. Cause: bitten right arm (teeth marks, Condy-washed) at 2am; odd nightly absences; no carriage orders.
- Paul's invitation: "Mrs. Dorcas Dene requests the pleasure... under the lamp-post... Berkeley Square."
- Midnight: Barraclough arrives by cab, latchkey.
- Dorcas's cabman: horse from St. Pancras yard; fare from Burton Crescent.
- Dorcas deduces left-hand hail; rose leaves on steps of a house in Burton Crescent.
- Neighbour woman: house empty; "gent... has taken the place."
- Next: burglary plan (Lady Anna to take keys from Barraclough's braces-chain, lantern signal, goloshes).
- Narrator takes keys from Lady Anna at doorstep; back to cab; two latchkeys.

## VIII. THE EMPTY HOUSE
- Dorcas: Barraclough surveillance; old Indian-looking man, white hair, gold spectacles, closely-cropped white moustache, came in 9pm.
- Van delivered brandy, hammers, nails, indiarubber mats, wire netting. Buyer **Mr. Aleem Mohammed** (white-haired "Indian"); notes changed at Charing Cross; year's rent paid in notes.
- Break-in: parlour; cupboard of ragged female clothes (red flannel petticoat, bonnet). Dorcas: "I wonder what he's done with the body?"
- Back kitchen: scullery sink; tallow; scraped labels; rusty chisel. Ghost of coffee.
- Front kitchen dresser; drawer handle with finger marks; bottles of **Hydrate of Chloral** (red "Poison" labels).
- Wine cellar: brandy cases; straw on stairs.
- First-floor back room locked; narrator forces door with jemmy. Inside: wire-netting cage. Woman (about 40, dark, once handsome), drugged, breathing; brandy bottle. Wedding ring, diamond ring, gold bangle.
- Dorcas: woman being killed by brandy and chloral; "this woman is probably his first wife."
- Dorcas scribbles note to doctor (Endsleigh Gardens). Narrator returns keys to Berkeley Square letter-box at 5:30am.
- Narrator leaves at dawn; sees the white-haired Indian crouching in doorway.

## IX. THE CLOTHES IN THE CUPBOARD
- Narrator: someone else left house during forced door; Indian escaped.
- Dorcas: Barraclough's accomplice = Aleem; Scotland Yard arrive.
- Doctor takes woman to hospital.
- **Inspector Stromberg** (CID) arrives. Dorcas sends telegram "All over. Come Crescent, ten to-night."
- Aleem's telegram warns Barraclough: "Don't go house. See me at once old place. Important. M."
- Woman: **Marian Judkins**; husband John Judkins (Jack); previous 10-year sentence for fraud; met her at the Empire; £50; invited her to Burton Crescent at midnight; chloroform; cage.
- Plan: Aleem is to take charge; Barraclough pays £5,000.
- 10pm: Barraclough enters. Aleem: "She died this morning early." Barraclough plans to strip corpse, dress it in rags, leave on doorstep as pauper.
- Corpse moves: "She's not dead!" Stromberg arrests Barraclough for attempted murder of wife Marian Judkins.
- Dorcas goes to tell Lady Anna she is free.

## X. THE HAVERSTOCK HILL MURDER
- Oak Tree Road shut ~6 weeks; Dorcas away with Paul and Mrs. Lester; letters forwarded to Jackson.
- Narrator at Kempton Park (February), with Inspector Swanage. Notes Flash George (fur coat, hundred-pound bets). Swanage: Dorcas on Hannaford case.
- Haverstock Hill murder, 5 January. Mrs. Hannaford beaten with poker in drawing-room. Husband Mr. Hannaford (stockjobber, 36) arrested at Paddington, then Broadmoor.
- Flash George seen ~100 yards away ~2:30am.
- Old Mrs. Hannaford (Uxbridge) hired Dorcas.
- Dorcas's Kempton disguise: gipsy race-card seller.
- Note traced: £100, number ²ₓ❘35421, Union Bank of London, from £5,000 cheque drawn by Mr. **Charles Drayson** (Mrs. Hannaford's first husband; died in Opéra Comique fire, Paris; watch found in ruins).
- Partner Thomas Holmes sentenced to 5 years' penal servitude.
- Narrator reveals: Dorcas was the gipsy race-card seller (Paul's "Nice or Monte Carlo"); Dorcas: "Give out" she was away.

## XI. THE BROWN BEAR LAMP
- Dorcas: notes not returned to bank before murder; several returned after.
- Dorcas refuses to tell police; carries case alone.
- Haverstock Hill house: caretaker (gardener). Front door sticks; cracks on opening.
- Dorcas's theory: Mrs. Hannaford came down thinking husband returned; struck from behind by intruder hiding behind brown bear lamp (bought by Drayson). Bear moved forward; carpet mark.
- Hidden slit in back of bear; hollow; bank-notes hidden inside.
- Drayson's escape: after Paris fire, returned as elderly man (grey beard, Inverness cape), using latchkey; Flash George kept watch.
- Flash George overheard at the Criterion: "Tell him Hungerford Bridge, midnight, Wednesday. Tell him to bring the lot and I'll cash up."
- Hungerford Bridge sting: Dorcas (Italian street musician) and Thomas Holmes (organ-grinder). Dorcas sings "Santa Lucia" as signal. Narrator seizes old man; false beard pulled off. Holmes identifies him as Drayson.
- Drayson plunges into Thames; dies in hospital. Confession: fled Paris, planned return for notes; struck Mrs. Hannaford to stop her alarming house.
- Flash George held with notes.
- Mr. Hannaford released from Broadmoor. Mrs. Hannaford's mother's letter thanks Dorcas.
- Dorcas: "These are the rewards of my profession."
